title: The 56 names whose daily refresh was refused, and every night the Hub Geiger held (3 Oct 2026, reconstructed from R2 and counters, not from the lost publisher log)
evidence_sources: R2 normalized/candidate_geiger_v1/_degraded/<timestamp>.json — one record per Geiger cycle that refused to publish (4,739 records, 18 Aug → 3 Oct 12:57Z)
R2 normalized/massive_provider_bars_deep_v1/D/<name>.json.gz for the 74 floor names — last-modified, first bar, history_cut stamp
R2 normalized/_history_cut_backup_v1/<run>/… — which objects each storage cut backed up (= cut)
R2 control/provider_tail_refresh_v1/receipts/… — 2,870 receipts of the live and scheduled bar passes (7 Sep → 3 Oct)
chart API /health per machine (counters since the 06:10 ET restart) and the bar service /metrics since 09:00 ET
Massive's grouped daily for 2026-10-02 vs the chart API's daily answer for all 590 names (first night of the second opinion)

timeline_et.what: The scheduled/live bar passes refuse 64 hourly cells per pass (13 names × 5 frames: BTDR, RSPC–RSPU, SERV): 'full provider replacement does not cover the existing history'. 15 passes.
timeline_et.cause: FR3 the replacement-coverage guard, before it tolerated a one-hour phase shift and bars before a floor. NOT the shorten guard. Fixed 28 Sep (image cut-f8e99f9).
timeline_et.served_wrong: No. Those cells stayed BEHIND (old bars served, named BEHIND in the receipts); nothing wrong-company.

timeline_et.what: Storage cut run cut-20260928: PL, SERV, SPIR, SYM cut at their floors, 57 objects backed up.
Admission v3 cuts 14 more names (ACMR AXON B HCA MRNA MTCH NET NU NVT NXT RUN S TLN XYZ) in both namespaces.
timeline_et.cause: cut-admission-v3 runs. These 18 names are the ones the bar service's floors file already knew; they never regrew.

timeline_et.what: H1 records 56 more floors in control/HISTORY_FLOORS.json (META V T MS GM NOW SNDK AGIX ALAB …).
Storage cut run cut-h1-20260929: 1,062 objects backed up and cut for 69 names, INCLUDING the deep daily (D) objects of all 56 (69 deep-D backups).
timeline_et.cause: H1's R2 cut. The chart API image carrying the floors (served-time cut) goes live about the same time.

timeline_et.what: The deep daily objects of the 56 names GROW BACK: the next forced daily refresh re-pulls each from 2003 and the shorten guard accepts a LONGER history. Evidence: on 3 Oct 09:00 ET the P11 cut removed 1,282 bars from AGIX's deep D (and similar for all 56) although cut-h1 had already cut that object on 29 Sep.
timeline_et.cause: BF3 + BF5 + FL1 together: the bar service was still on image cut-f8e99f9 whose floors file lacked the 56, so clampFromToFloor did nothing; the request was widened back to the object's unchanged requested_from (2003); a longer pull passes the shorten guard. The 16:15 ET ACQUIRED_BEFORE_DAILY_FINALIZATION trigger is the first forced refresh after the cut.
timeline_et.served_wrong: No: the chart API cut at serving time (FL3) since 05:49Z, so no chart or Geiger input showed the earlier company. Storage carried it again.

timeline_et.what: All four batch machines, the bar service included, move to live-112d10c, which carries the 56 floors.

First refusal: the midnight daily refresh (NOT_ACQUIRED_TODAY_ET) asks the bar service for META & co. from their floors; the stored deep D starts in 2003 again; 'provider acquisition would shorten existing history'. The Geiger publisher's D rung for 56 names returns 503 DAILY_REFRESH_UNAVAILABLE; the publisher refuses the whole 590-name artifact (SYMBOL_FAILURES / UNIVERSE_INCOMPLETE).
timeline_et.cause: BF5 × FL1 × CA1/CA2 × GP1 (the P11 deadlock, amplified by the all-or-nothing publication rule).

timeline_et.what: 240 refused cycles. The Hub shows the Geiger reading from 29 Sep ~20:00 ET all day, through the whole trading session. Between 06:14 and 08:45 a second cause stacks: 115 names fail on 6h SOURCE_BAR_FINALITY_UNPROVEN (returned 475).
timeline_et.cause: As above; the 6h episode is the finality receipt (FIN1/GS2), a separate rule.
timeline_et.served_wrong: Stale, not wrong: every served number was a real reading; it was the previous evening's.

timeline_et.what: The post-close live pass refreshes the 1D cells of all 590 names through the tail-refresh path (10,030-cell DUE_FRAME passes) and rewrites the deep D objects with a fresh acquisition stamp. The daily-refresh policy now says CURRENT, the chart API stops asking the bar service, the 56 names' D rung serves, the Geiger publishes 590/590 again.
timeline_et.cause: DC1/TR4 'cure' CA1 by accident each evening; the deadlock is only hidden until midnight.

timeline_et.what: 80 refused cycles (cycles stretch to ~12 minutes because 56 names × 9 retries). Same stale-all-day pattern. Evening: published again.

106 refused cycles, same cause. 16:11 → 20:00: 52 more cycles refused for a DIFFERENT reason: 1–2 rungs ABSENT (returned 590, PARTICIPATING_RUNG_ABSENT) — an intraday rung behind the daily reference for one or two names holds the whole artifact.
timeline_et.cause: GS3 × GP1: one absent rung anywhere = nothing published.

timeline_et.what: 135 refused cycles (coordinator's 42 from 06:13 are the tail of these). 06:10 the chart API moves to p10; 06:11 the publisher restarts (log emptied). Chart API machine 811d…: 30,636 daily refresh attempts, 50 successes, between 06:10 and 09:00.
timeline_et.cause: Same deadlock; on Saturday nothing refreshes the 1D cells after the close, so it would have held all weekend.

timeline_et.what: Bar service → p11-8dc23b6: the stored object is cut at its floor before the comparison; 56 names refresh within 40 s; every cycle since 09:01 publishes 590/590, 4,130/4,130; the Geiger candidate at 10:32 ET is VERIFIED.
timeline_et.cause: P11 (FL2). The 56 deep D objects now carry history_cut { cut_by: 'provider-bar-fetch/getBars', cut_utc: 2026-10-03T13:00–13:01Z }.

timeline_et.what: Second opinion, first night: Massive's grouped daily for 2 Oct (12,601 rows) vs our daily answer for all 590 names: 590 served, 590 last bar = 2 Oct, 590 closes EXACTLY equal.

answers.since_when_did_the_56_fail: From 30 Sep 00:02 ET, the first forced daily refresh after the bar service learned the 56 floors (23:23 ET 29 Sep). Each day it failed from 00:00 ET until the post-close pass rewrote the daily objects (~16:13–16:30 ET), then worked until midnight.
answers.on_which_nights_did_the_geiger_hold: Daytime, not night: 30 Sep 00:02–16:26, 1 Oct 00:04–16:26, 2 Oct 00:06–16:36 and 16:11–20:00 (different cause), 3 Oct 00:05–08:57. Before this episode: whole days 9–10, 12–16, 19–21 Sep (360 refused cycles a day), 25 Sep (247), 26 Sep 00:08–02:30 (every name, DURABLE_HISTORY_CATCHUP_REQUIRED on 2h), 29 Sep 06:03–08:56 (62 names, 6h finality), 29 Sep 16:22 (1 rung absent).
answers.was_anything_served_from_stale_or_wrong_: Wrong-company: no — the chart API has cut at serving time since 29 Sep 01:49 ET (FL3), and the Geiger reads the chart API. Stale: yes — during every hold the Hub Geiger showed the last complete reading with no visible age: up to 16.5 hours old during three full trading sessions (30 Sep, 1 Oct, 2 Oct). The daily CHART for the 56 names answered 503 (no chart) rather than a stale chart during those hours.
answers.are_the_24_25_sep_64_failed_cells_the_sa: No. Those were the replacement-coverage guard (FR3) refusing a one-hour phase shift on BTDR, the RSP* funds and SERV (13 names × 5 hourly frames = 64–65 cells, 15 passes, 27 Sep 22:20 → 28 Sep 09:18 ET), fixed on 28 Sep. The 25–26 Sep failures before them (56, 100 and 280 cells per pass) were a third thing: 'frame must be one of …' — a frame object handed to a function that wanted a token (fixed bb57891). The P11 entry's guess that they were the shorten guard is corrected here.
answers.why_the_counters_lied: The bar service counted every /acquire failure as provider_errors and the chart API threw the bar service's detail away. 181,463 of our own refusals read as Massive's fault. Fixed on this branch: one named cause per failure, counted by name, detail relayed.

most_dangerous_interactions: BF5 (never shorter) × FL1 (never before the floor) × BF3 (widen to the old requested_from): right alone, a deadlock together — and the OPPOSITE failure (regrow the old company) when the floor is missing from one image. Rule: the floor must live in the DATA (the object says where it begins), not only in an image.

CA1/CA2 (refresh at midnight, refuse to serve on failure) × GP1 (publish nothing unless everything computed): one name's refusal silences 590 names' Geiger for the whole trading day, and the Hub shows no age.
GP2 (retry 3 × 3) × a deterministic refusal: 56 names × 9 attempts per cycle = ~3 requests a second against the bar service for days, each a wasted Massive pull, each counted as a provider error.
DC1 (post-close 1D pass rewrites deep D) × CA1 (acquired today = current): the evening pass hides the morning's deadlock, so the failure looks intermittent and nobody sees a 3-day pattern.

SY2 (universe digest baked into images and env) × every reader: an admission that moves most pins but not all splits the estate silently; the Geiger boot file is injected by machine config, not by the image.
